details: CONFIRMED. relay_gate.run calls refuse_bad_settings(worktree) on every gate, and the relay on PATH
(~/.local/bin/relay -> ~/relay/bin/relay) imports ~/relay/lib, i.e. master's relay_kit after the merge, whatever the lane's own
code is. The new RENAMED branch in parse() turns the old key into a problem, so every branch still holding master's pre-merge
kit.toml is refused. Running this branch's refuse_bad_settings on the live lane worktree
.worktrees/a-sigterm-in-a-gate-does-not-name-its-sender reproduces it. 19 of the 20 wt/* branches hold `max_parallel`. The
message's next step, `relay setup`, run inside a lane worktree also rewrites settings.json, .gitignore and the projects.toml
registration (seen in the probe's done list), which is not what a lane should do; the right step for a lane is to take the
default branch. "Work goes on while the owner is away" lanes would each stop on a red gate after this lands: ordinary use
fails, so HIGH. The brief asks that an old name be refused; this keeps that for files that wrote the old name, and only spares
(or redirects) branches that inherited it.
Size: 30 minutes.
evidence: REFUSED: settings problem in the branch's .claude/kit.toml: .claude/kit.toml [delegate] max_parallel is an old name; it is now max_agents_per_change (`relay setup` renames it)
$ for b in wt/*: git show $b:.claude/kit.toml | grep -q '^max_parallel'
failing_case: Master after this merge: bin/relay (the main checkout's lib, used for every worktree's gate) refuses any kit.toml problem.
A lane branch cut before the merge, e.g. wt/a-sigterm-in-a-gate-does-not-name-its-sender, carries master's old
.claude/kit.toml `[delegate] max_parallel = 6` and has not touched it. Its next `relay gate` (the cycle gates the branch head
before the check) now raises GateRefused: "settings problem in the branch's .claude/kit.toml: .claude/kit.toml [delegate]
max_parallel is an old name; it is now max_agents_per_change (`relay setup` renames it)".
Should: a branch whose old name came unchanged from the default branch is not stopped by a rename it never made (or, at the
least, the refusal names the step that fixes it in a lane: take the default branch), and setup-registered projects keep the
loud refusal.
fix_hint: In relay_gate.refuse_bad_settings, drop the RENAMED problems when the branch's kit.toml line is the one of the merge-base with
the default branch (the branch did not write it), or simplest: make the RENAMED message say "run `relay setup` (in a task
branch: take the default branch)" and have the gate accept a renamed key only when the default branch's own kit.toml still has
it. Either way add the fixture test of pass-case 1.
pass_cases: 1. A git fixture: master commits kit.toml "[delegate]\nmax_parallel = 6\n"; branch "task" forks; master renames it to
max_agents_per_change; relay_gate.run(task worktree) on the unchanged branch is not refused for the renamed key (or its
refusal text contains "take the default branch"), per the chosen fix.
2. The same branch after it takes master by a merge commit: kit.toml has max_agents_per_change = 6 and the gate passes the
settings step.
3. A branch that itself writes `typed_only = false` into kit.toml is still refused, naming typed_agents_only
(tests/test_kit_schema.py keeps passing).
4. relay_kit.parse('[delegate]\nmax_parallel = 4\n').problems still names max_agents_per_change (doctor and the route guard
keep reporting it).
reason: tests/test_kit_rename_fixes.py LaneBranch tests (inherited name says take the default branch; after merge passes; own write still refused; parse names new key); first fails at base.
findings.summary: after the merge every lane branch not yet on master is refused by the gate: its kit.toml still says max_parallel (19 of 20 wt/* branches), and the refusal names relay setup, the wrong next step in a lane

person reaches it by following the refusal ("it is now max_agents_per_change") by adding a line, or by a merge that brings the
new key next to an old one. The result is a kit.toml the gate refuses as unreadable and the route guard runs on defaults.
Size: 15 minutes.
evidence: ['.claude/kit.toml cannot be read: Cannot overwrite a value (at line 3, column 26); used the defaults']

details: Question for the owner. What it is about: the cap on agents that run at once. How it works: before each Agent call the route
guard counts the agents running in this session in today's ledger and adds a note (not a refusal) when the count reaches the
cap. Live example: relay builds 6 changes at once in one front session; with max_agents_per_change = 6 the note comes as soon
as each change has one agent, not when one change has 6. The owner suggested max_parallel_agents_per_change; the front chose
max_agents_per_change (owner can reverse). Answers: (a) rename to max_agents_at_once and say "in this session" in the
comment: name matches the count, drops the "per change" wording of the rule; (b) keep the name and make the guard count per
change: needs the ledger to know each agent's change, a bigger change; (c) keep as is.
Size: 5 minutes for (a).
evidence: plugins/delegate/hooks/route-guard.py:301 running = running_now(data.get("session_id")); if running >= int(cfg["max_agents_per_change"])
failing_case: Relay's own kit.toml sets max_agents_per_change = 6 (it was max_parallel = 6, matching 6 lanes). The guard
(route-guard.py:301-306) notes once 6 agents run in the session, summed over every change the front is building. A person
reading the name expects 6 agents in each change.
fix_hint: (a): rename in RENAMED/SCHEMA/route-guard/docs and the setup comment.
pass_cases: 1. Artifact: the key's name and its setup comment say the same unit the guard counts (session or change).
2. Artifact: docs/delegation.md "Parallelism" says which one is counted.
reason: Question for the owner (name vs what the guard counts); the fixer left it open, I agree it is the owner's call.
findings.summary: max_agents_per_change names a per-change cap, but the route guard counts agents running in the whole session
